case: Northbridge Renewables Limited v Meridian Components Limited

exhibits.citation_text: I refer to the executed Supply Agreement dated 1 February 2026, exhibited to this statement as AH1.
Northbridge issued its implementing purchase order on 3 February. A copy of Purchase Order NRL-1047 is at exhibit AH2.

exhibits.description: Email chain - delivery dates and processor allocation
exhibits.citation_text: By an email sent on 5 February, Mr Reeve confirmed the two delivery dates and stated that processor allocation was complete. That email and my reply are exhibited together as AH3.
The agreed minutes of that meeting record those assurances. I refer to the minutes marked AH4.

exhibits.description: Email chain - processor shortage and delay
exhibits.citation_text: The 18 March email chain, in which I asked why the shortage had not been disclosed earlier, is exhibited as AH5.
On 25 March, Northbridge sent a formal notice requiring Meridian to provide a recovery plan and confirm cure by 1 April. I refer to that notice of delay as exhibit AH6.

exhibits.description: Email chain - thermal shutdowns and processor substitution
exhibits.citation_text: That quality-warning email and Meridian's response are exhibited as AH7.
I refer to Verity's inspection report dated 22 April, exhibited as AH8.
On 30 April, Northbridge terminated the supply agreement for material delay and non-conformity. The termination letter is exhibited as AH9.
Apex charged GBP 520,000 for 40 expedited replacement units, including expedited freight. Its invoice AC-7782 dated 5 May is exhibited as AH10.
